schemes.name: butterfly_field_wide_lanes
schemes.secondary_language: five three-storey pavilions under butterfly roofs, spread wider so no two plans touch, tied by a low shared ground plate
schemes.formal_principle: The field of V roofs is kept and the lanes are made real: spread 1.8 opens every gap to a lane a person walks down, and a low tie plate under the five gives the field one ground and one address.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a field of V roofs on one tie plate
schemes.reference_basis: development of field_under_butterfly_wings: the field of V roofs is kept; the jury's overlap, frontage and core remarks are answered
schemes.design_argument_ko: 겹치던 평면을 벌려 골목을 만들고 낮은 공용 판이 다섯을 하나의 밭으로 묶는다.

ops.why: Spread 1.8 answers the overlapping plans: every pavilion stands clear; tie 0.3 gives the cluster one shared ground plate so the field reads as one project.
Every roof still folds inward as a butterfly - the valley is the idea and is kept in every child.

schemes.name: butterfly_field_with_a_canopy
schemes.secondary_language: five pavilions under butterfly roofs, a shared canopy reaching toward the open side as the field's front
schemes.formal_principle: A field needs a front: the pavilions keep their valleys, and one canopy reaches out toward the open side so the street reads an entry and the cluster gains the frontage hierarchy the jury missed.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a field of V roofs with a front canopy
schemes.reference_basis: development of field_under_butterfly_wings: the field of V roofs is kept; the jury's overlap, frontage and core remarks are answered
schemes.design_argument_ko: 열린 변으로 뻗는 캐노피가 밭에 정면과 입구를 준다.

ops.why: Five pavilions kept at the parent's scale; tie 0.2 adds a thin shared ground.
Every roof still folds inward as a butterfly - the valley is the idea and is kept in every child.
A canopy toward the open side gives the field a front and an entry the jury said it lacked.

schemes.name: butterfly_field_toward_the_street
schemes.secondary_language: five pavilions under butterfly roofs, the whole field pushed toward the open side so it fronts the street
schemes.formal_principle: A field needs a front: the pavilions keep their valleys and the cluster moves toward the open side, so the street meets the first pavilions instead of a leftover strip - the frontage hierarchy the jury missed.
schemes.reference_basis: development of field_under_butterfly_wings: the field of V roofs is kept; the jury's overlap, frontage and core remarks are answered
schemes.design_argument_ko: 밭 전체를 열린 변으로 밀어 거리가 첫 파빌리온과 만나게 한다.

ops.why: Five pavilions spread 1.7 so plans clear; a tie plate is the court floor.
Every roof still folds inward as a butterfly - the valley is the idea and is kept in every child.
The field grows toward the open side so its front reaches the street; the west tip stops being empty.

schemes.name: butterfly_field_of_four_lifted
schemes.secondary_language: four larger pavilions under butterfly roofs, lifted on supports so the whole ground is one public field
schemes.formal_principle: Fewer, larger houses and a free ground: four pavilions give each a floor plate that takes a core, and lifting them makes the ground under the field continuous - the public room the gaps only hinted at.
schemes.dominant_gesture: four lifted V-roof pavilions over one ground
schemes.reference_basis: development of field_under_butterfly_wings: the field of V roofs is kept; the jury's overlap, frontage and core remarks are answered
schemes.design_argument_ko: 네 채로 줄여 코어를 넣고, 들어 올려 지면 전체를 공용 밭으로 만든다.

ops.why: Four pavilions answer the core-per-house remark: each plate is large enough for its own core.
Lifting frees the ground as one continuous public field under the roofs.
Shallower valleys so the top floor is not cut by the pitch, as the jury noted; said after the lift so the raised houses carry them.
